$comment: Slot type schema for the Talent One kit. Generated from the nine templates' shipped worked examples by scripts/extract_slot_schema.py, then hand-corrected (22 slots) where the inferred type from a single example was ambiguous. Consumed by scripts/check_fill.py's --types pass: a filled artifact's slot value is checked against this file's `type`, not just checked for presence. Regenerating this file from a new example set will overwrite hand corrections; diff before committing a regeneration.

types.label: A short name, title, or tag. Free text, but stays inside the example's word-count band.
types.prose_short: A sentence or two of body copy. Voice rules apply (no em dash, no forbidden phrases).
types.prose_long: A paragraph of body copy. Same voice rules; respects the density budget in FILL_SPEC S3.5.
types.count: A bare number, optionally "~", a thousands comma, and a K/M/B suffix. Example: "~1.7M", "150K".
types.count_range: Two counts joined by a hyphen or en dash. Example: "1,800-2,400".
types.currency: A dollar figure, optionally "~" and a K/M suffix. Example: "$154K".
types.currency_range: Two dollar figures joined by a hyphen or en dash, optionally with a short qualifier prefix or suffix where a slot's own word band allows it (e.g. an "Example:" prefix or a "+ equity" suffix). Example: "$120-145K".
types.ratio: Two numbers joined by a colon. Example: "3:1".
types.duration: A time span or relative timeframe. Example: "2 business days", "D14", "45 min".
types.date: A month/year, bare year, or ISO date. Example: "JUN 2025".
types.pill: One of the provenance words: Sourced, Estimate, Modeled, Internal, Derived. Never anything else.
types.chip: A value from a small controlled vocabulary specific to that slot (see its note). Never invent a new chip value.
types.empty_cell: A bare hyphen or en dash meaning "no data for this cell". Distinct from data-optional: the row stays, this one field is empty.
types.delta: A before -> after transition. Both sides are required.
types.metric: A single large numeric headline stat. Core must be numeric; unit varies by context (%, x multiplier, K/M count) and is not fixed to one type. Example: "0.4%", "5x".
